previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex medical history including Crohn’s disease, SVC syndrome, and PTSD was admitted for high fevers, nausea, vomiting, and recurrent right thigh pain following a recent hospitalization for a groin hematoma and SVC recanalization. Initial concern was recurrence of the hematoma, but ultrasound showed complete resolution. A CT scan revealed no Crohn’s flare or bowel obstruction but identified a small 3 cm fluid collection in the right thigh, likely a minor hematoma. The patient was managed with an NG tube for gastric dysmotility and IV medications for pain, nausea, and anxiety. She remained afebrile after admission, and extensive workup found no infectious source. Symptoms improved with supportive care, and she was discharged on a taper of Dilaudid and diphenhydramine, with instructions for port care, medication management, and follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
#Fevers: Patient was afebrile for most of her admission, with 
only low grade temps in the ___ while in house. Noted to

was no tenderness or erythema around the port site on exam. She 
had no evidence of UTI, C. difficile infection, or CMV/EBV 
infection (CMV titers negative, had a positive monospot w/ 
splenomegaly, but her EBV titers were consistent with a previous 
infection of mononucleosis.) ID was consulted for treatment of 
her bacteremia. Sensitives from the OSH blood cultures were sent

radiology_notes.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

HISTORY:  ___ woman with Crohn's disease, ? gas in urine, possible
fistula, lower abdominal pain.  Please evaluate for fistula and evaluate for
acute process.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial imaging was performed from the lung bases through
the pubic symphysis following administration of oral contrast.  IV contrast
was not administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also
prepared.

CT OF ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  Within the right lower lobe of the lung,
there is a 7-mm ground glass nodule which is new from CT performed 1 month
ago. Given the short interval between the two studies, this likely represents
an infectious and/or inflammatory process.  The remainder of the lungs are
clear and there are no pleural effusions.

There is mild splenomegaly at 16 cm in long axis.  On this noncontrast study,
the kidneys, adrenals, liver, and gallbladder are all unremarkable.  The
pancreas is normal in appearance. There are scattered retroperitoneal and
mesenteric lymph nodes, but none enlarged by CT criteria. The abdominal loops
of small and large bowel and stomach are unremarkable.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST.  Patient is status post right
hemicolectomy and there is suture material seen within the right upper
quadrant.  There is contrast opacification through the rectum. There is no
evidence for fistula or bowel obstruction. Several loops of small bowel are
matted to the right lower anterior abdominal wall likely post-surgical. There
is no free air or free fluid. The urinary bladder is normal in appearance
containing no gas or enteric contrast. There are no pathologically enlarged
pelvic or inguinal lymph nodes. Patient is status post hysterectomy and
oophorectomy. The vaginal cuff is normal in appearance.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no suspicious sclerotic or lytic lesions identified.
There is a healed incisional scar seen within the lower abdominal and pelvic
midline related to patient's prior bowel surgery. Calcifications are noted in
the buttocks.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No evidence for fistula or bowel obstruction.  Patient is status post
right hemi-colectomy.
2.  New right lower lobe ground glass nodule, likely inflammatory or
infectious given that it is new since 1 month prior CT.
3.  Splenomegaly, which is new compared to prior examination. Recommend
clinical correlation.

INDICATION:  Patient with history of Crohn's disease with fever and
bacteremia.  Assess for extravasation of contrast into bladder.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis of the same day at 07:35.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images through the pelvis were obtained without
IV contrast.  Residual oral contrast is seen within the colon, and no
additional oral contrast was administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted
images were generated.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:  Oral contrast is seen within the sigmoid colon
and within the rectum.  No oral contrast or air is seen within the bladder.
The patient is post hysterectomy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis. There
is soft tissue thickening of the anterior abdominal wall at the midline, which
may represent scar tissue related to prior surgeries.  Small bowel is seen
just deep to the abdominal wall at this locale.  Calcified granulomas are seen
within the subcutaneous tissues of the buttocks.  No nodes meeting criteria
for pathologic enlargement are seen within the pelvis or inguinal regions.

BONE WINDOWS:  There are no suspicious osteolytic or sclerotic lesions.  There
is sclerosis of the iliac side of the sacroiliac joints bilaterally, greater
on the right.

IMPRESSION:  There is no high-density material or air in the bladder to
suggest an enterovesical fistula.  The sigmoid colon and rectum are opacified
with oral contrast.  No free pelvic fluid.

LEFT FOREARM, THREE VIEWS

INDICATION:  Crohn's disease, now with bacteremia.  Ecchymosis.  Evaluate for
fracture.

FINDINGS:  No comparisons.  No acute fracture or dislocation is seen.  No
lucent or sclerotic lesion is noted.  Osseous alignment is preserved.  Soft
tissues are otherwise unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

No acute fracture or dislocation.

ADDENDUM:

In the body of the report, the size of the fluid collection should read 6 x 9
x 18 mm.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with Crohn's disease as well as septicemia and
subacute pelvic pain for three weeks.  History of right groin hematoma status
post resolution by imaging.

COMPARISON:  ___, CT of the pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired on a 3 Tesla
magnet.  Dynamic series were acquired before, during, and after the uneventful
intravenous administration of 0.1 mmol/kg of gadolinium-DTPA.  Multiplanar
reformations were produced on a separate workstation.

FINDINGS:  The bladder, rectum, and visualized bowel appear unremarkable.  The
patient is status post hysterectomy.  There is a small amount of free fluid in
the pelvis.

In the right pectineus muscles, there is an oval-shaped fluid collection
measuring 6.9 x 18 mm hypointense on T2-weighted images with surrounding rim
of low signal, and edema within the muscle belly of the pectineus.  Post-
contrast, there is thick peripheral enhancement.  There are mildly prominent
lymph nodes within the right inguinal and right external iliac chains.  There
is minimal fat stranding in the area adjacent to the right common femoral
vessels, presumably where the prior hematoma (no longer seen) was located. The
signal within the bone marrow is probably within normal limits. Apparently
minimally elevated signal in the right lesser trochanter (3:41) on the edge of
the field of view and felt to  be artifactual.  The remainder of the muscles
appear symmetric in bulk and of normal signal.  The scout images demonstrate a
low signal focus in the right greater trochanter which was seen on the CT and
is consistent with a bone island.  Reformations were essential in delineating
the anatomy.

IMPRESSION:  Small peripherally enhancing fluid collection within the right
pectineus muscle is compatible with an abscess.  Given the small size,
followup MRI after appropriate treatment is recommended to asses for
resolution.

and right thigh pain.  Evaluate for new abscess or extension.

clear.  There is no pleural effusion.  Visualized heart and pericardium are

The liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, left kidney, and right kidney are

A moderate amount of debris is seen within the stomach.  Otherwise, stomach,
